classification.difficultyReason: Use the mean to find the sum of two missing integers, then apply strict ordering to enumerate all possible pairs.

content.prompt: The numbers $5, 12, 16, x, y, 24, 30$ have mean $18$. If $x$ and $y$ are positive integers and the numbers are arranged from smallest to largest with no two numbers the same, find the possible values of $x$ and $y$.

answer.short:
$(x,y)=(17,22),\ (18,21),\ (19,20)$.

The missing numbers sum to $39$ and satisfy $16<x<y<24$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Sum of all seven numbers}&=7\times18=126\\\text{Sum of the known numbers}&=5+12+16+24+30=87\\x+y&=126-87\\x+y&=39\end{align*}$$

The stated order and distinct values require $16<x<y<24$. Since $x<y$ and their sum is $39$, $x$ can only be $17$, $18$ or $19$.

$$\begin{aligned}x=17:&\quad y=39-17=22\\x=18:&\quad y=39-18=21\\x=19:&\quad y=39-19=20\end{aligned}$$

Thus the possible pairs are $(17,22)$, $(18,21)$ and $(19,20)$. Each pair satisfies the strict order and gives a total of $126$, so the mean is $18$.
